er.title: Energy Recharge Calculator
er.intro: Runs the current rotation for {{laps}} laps in gcsim and finds the total Energy Recharge (ER%) needed for every character's burst. It collects the requirement for each span between bursts (a window) and shows it in three levels.
er.stale: The party or rotation has changed since the last calculation, so the previous result is hidden. Press “Start calculation” to recalculate.
er.oldVersion: This result was computed with gcsim {{saved}} (now {{current}}). Please recalculate.
er.errorMismatch: Even with very high ER, burst timing does not match the baseline (run ignoring energy). Bursts are shifted for a reason other than energy.
er.note:
The number in parentheses is the share of bursts that can fire without waiting for energy.
Typical and Stable are “measured”: the share of tried bursts that fired without waiting at that value.
Certain is an “estimate”: when every tried burst fired without waiting, it is N/(N+1) (the next untried burst exceeds the maximum with probability 1/(N+1)).
The share is per burst, so even at Stable not every burst over several laps is guaranteed to fire without waiting.
Use Certain if no burst may wait.
The “[-…% to +…%]” under Typical and Stable is the error from the number of seeds tried.
The “[min -…%]” under Certain means the actual value can be lower than shown by up to this much.
er.elapsedRunningRange: Elapsed {{elapsed}} / about {{low}}–{{high}} left (rough; longer if verification drags on)
er.phaseRefine: Verifying the Typical and Stable values in gcsim
er.phaseVerify: Verifying the Certain values in gcsim
er.colTypicalTitle: Enough for 70% of the bursts. A rough guide for real play
er.colStableTitle: Enough for 90% of the bursts. Occasionally a lap falls short
er.colCertainTitle: Enough for every collected burst (100%; verified in gcsim). Works even with the worst luck, so it reads high because it picks the worst random window
er.colCurrentTitle: Energy Recharge calculated by gcsim from the current settings (owned build & stats, or defaults), including weapon, character and artifact set bonuses. Green: at or above the certain value; yellow: at or above the stable value; red: below
er.enemyParticles: Enemy particles (non-elemental particles from enemies, crystals, drops, etc.)
er.precisionNote: The Certain value is verified by running everyone at that value in gcsim and checking that no burst slips, narrowing it down (Rough to 10% ER steps, Precise to 1% steps; Precise takes longer). Typical and Stable are verified the same way only for parties with Raiden Shogun, Kujou Sara or Dori. All are values within the seeds tried.
er.verifyAuto: This party includes {{names}}. Their recovery depends on their own ER, so Typical and Stable are also re-derived by running everyone at those values in gcsim (verified like the Certain value). It takes longer.
er.coresNote: Number of cores (parallel Workers) used for the calculation (1–{{max}}, default {{def}}; saved on this device). More cores are faster but with diminishing returns, and use more memory (several hundred MB per core) and heat the CPU. This applies when calculating in the browser (WASM).
er.seedsNote: Random outcomes (particles etc.) are tried with seeds 1 to this number (1–{{max}}, default 20). More seeds get closer to the true value and raise the Certain probability, but time grows in proportion. The same settings and count always give the same result.
er.burstWaitNote: When a burst lacks energy, it counts as enough if the burst can go off within this many seconds once particles arrive (0.1 s steps; default 0 s). The longer it is, the lower and steadier the required ER. Raise it only if you can wait in real play.
er.introAbyss: Runs the current rotation (opening + loop) in gcsim for the length of the battle, matching an Abyss fight, and finds the total Energy Recharge (ER%) needed for every character's burst. Everyone starts with 0 energy and the first burst is judged too. Use it to check that the looping bursts can go off every time.
er.abyssBanner: Abyss mode: calculates with start energy 0, timed particles and the battle length. Results are saved separately from normal mode.
er.battleSecondsNote: The rotation (opening + loop) repeats until this time is over (the number of loops is chosen automatically; the last loop may run past the battle length). The rotation length is estimated from the action durations.
er.firstBurstWait: The first burst may wait up to
er.firstBurstWaitNote: Everyone starts with 0 energy, so the first burst is delayed until enough particles arrive. It counts as enough if it can go off within this many seconds of its planned time (0.5 s steps; default 0.5 s). If the opening (first lap only) uses skills only to build burst energy, the default 0.5 s is enough. If the opening itself fires a burst, no amount of ER lets it go off at the planned time and the result is "Unreachable", so raise this value. Later bursts use "Wait before a burst" below.
er.timedParticlesNote: Particles that appear at a fixed time from the start of the battle (for example when a boss shield breaks; up to {{max}}). They are handled like enemy particles: Energy Recharge applies, and the on-field character gets more than the ones on the bench. They are calculated as colorless particles (elemental particles cannot be expressed).
er.particleLimitTimed: [Limitation] gcsim can use only one particle setting. Because there are {{n}} timed particles, only the latest one ({{seconds}} s) is used in the calculation; the other {{ignored}} are ignored.
er.particleLimitPeriodic: [Limitation] Because there are timed particles, the enemy's periodic particles are not used in the calculation (gcsim can use only one particle setting).
er.adjustTimed: {{n}} of the {{total}} timed particles cannot be passed to gcsim (gcsim can use only one particle setting), so the app adds them to the Energy timeline itself.
er.adjustInvulnerable: There are {{n}} no-damage periods (set on the DPS screen). During them, energy that requires dealing damage (Favonius-type particles, Dehya's Skill particles, Albedo C1, Klee A4, Rosaria C4, Crane's Echoing Call, Moonglow, Katsuragikiri Nagamasa, Lumidouce Elegy, Traveler (Cryo) C1, Mika C4) is removed from the Energy timeline. The Sacrificial Skill cooldown reset is not adjusted.
er.adjustNoVerify: Because the timeline is adjusted, the final check run in gcsim is not done (the result is "calculation only". For teams with Raiden Shogun, Kujou Sara or Dori, the recovery that depends on other characters' ER is not reflected, so the required ER comes out low). "Burst timing check" runs in gcsim only, so only the latest one of the timed particles is used there.
er.adjustedResult: This result is a "calculation only" value obtained by the app adjusting the timeline ({{timed}} timed particles added, {{windows}} no-damage periods). It was not checked in gcsim.
er.abyssResultCondition: Conditions of this result: battle {{battle}} s, first burst may wait {{first}} s, {{timed}} timed particle entries
er.abyssConditionChanged: The current battle conditions differ from those this result was calculated with. Press Start to calculate again.
er.timingTitle: Burst timing with the current build
er.timingNote: Runs the rotation as it is now (no extra ER) from 0 energy for the whole battle time, and shows how many seconds each burst is late compared with its planned time (the time when burst energy is ignored), as the maximum over the seeds tried. A delay within {{sec}} s counts as on time. When a burst is late, the actions after it shift by the same amount, so the delays add up. It does not use the ER calculation result, so you can check it without calculating first.
er.timingNone: There is no burst within the battle time
er.timingFirstLate: First burst: planned {{planned}} s → actually {{from}}-{{to}} s
er.timingFirstMissed: First burst: planned {{planned}} s. It never goes off in some seeds ({{missed}} / {{total}})
er.timingSummary: {{ok}} of {{total}} bursts are on time in every seed
er.timingChipTitle: Burst {{n}}: planned {{planned}} s. Delay: median {{median}} s, max {{max}} s. On time in {{onTime}} / {{total}} seeds, missed in {{missed}}
er.timingChipTitleMissed: Burst {{n}}: planned {{planned}} s. Does not go off in time in {{missed}} / {{total}} seeds
er.presetsNote: Save the current battle conditions (battle time, first-burst wait, timed particles, enemy particles, enemy settings, enemy-state periods) under a name and call them up later (for example one per boss; up to {{max}}). Click a name to put its conditions into the fields. Saving under the same name overwrites it. They are included in the backup. Shared by the charge-efficiency calc and the DPS calc.
er.presetLoadTitle: Put these conditions into the fields below
er.presetSummary: Battle {{battle}} s, first-burst wait {{first}} s, {{timed}} timed particles, {{enemies}} enemies, {{states}} enemy-state periods
er.presetOverwriteConfirm: "{{name}}" is already saved. Overwrite it with the current conditions?
er.presetFull: You can save up to {{max}} battle conditions. Delete some before saving a new one.
er.presetSaveFailed: Could not save (the storage on this device may be full)
er.enemyParticlesNote: The default is 1 particle every 5–8 s (gcsim's official example is every 8–12 s). Set the count to 0 for no enemy particles. Adjust it to your fight.
er.errorVerify: Could not settle the Certain value within the verification limit. Review the party or rotation, or try again.

dps.staleCondition: The battle conditions, enemy settings, enemy-state periods or the mode have changed since this was calculated. This result is from before the change.
dps.energyNoteOnAbyss: A burst that lacks energy waits until it has enough (the time stretches accordingly). The start energy is 0. Particles follow the battle conditions (the timed particles and the enemy's periodic particles set in the charge-efficiency screen).
dps.title: DPS Calc
dps.intro: Runs the current party and rotation in gcsim many times (different seeds) for the opening + N loops, and shows the average damage per second (DPS), its spread and each character's share. Crits and other randomness make single runs vary, so more runs give a steadier value.
dps.abyssNotice: Abyss mode is on. The battle conditions (battle time, timed particles, the enemy's periodic particles) are shared with the charge-efficiency calc and cannot be changed here (change them in the charge-efficiency screen). When burst energy is taken into account, it starts from 0 energy. DPS = damage up to the end of the battle ÷ battle time. The enemy settings and the enemy-state periods are set on this screen.
dps.abyssCondition: Current battle conditions (shared with the charge-efficiency calc)
dps.abyssConditionSummary: Battle {{battle}} s, {{timed}} timed particles, enemy particles: {{amount}} every {{min}}–{{max}} s
dps.abyssConditionNoEnergy: (Burst energy is not taken into account, so the start energy and particles are not used.)
dps.loopsAbyss: The number of rotation laps is decided automatically from the battle time ({{battle}} s): the number of laps at which the opening plus the loops exceed the battle time.
dps.lastRunAbyss: Last calculation: battle {{battle}} s ({{loops}} rotation laps), {{runs}} runs ({{seconds}} s)
dps.totalDamageAbyss: Total damage up to {{seconds}} s of battle: {{total}} (average) ÷ battle time
dps.battleShort: In {{count}} of {{runs}} runs the rotation did not last until the end of the battle. Those runs are calculated over the time they lasted.
dps.stateAdjust: Enemy-state correction: {{amount}} ({{percent}}% of the total damage before the correction)
dps.statesNote: Set periods, in seconds from the start of the battle, in which the enemy takes no damage or its resistances change (up to {{max}}; start inclusive, end exclusive). They cannot be passed to gcsim, so the damage log is corrected after the calculation. In a no-damage period the damage becomes 0. A resistance change multiplies the damage of each listed element by (the multiplier for the new resistance ÷ the multiplier for the resistance in the enemy settings); this is an approximation that ignores resistance-shred effects. Particles are not corrected (they still appear during a no-damage period, as gcsim produces them).
dps.stateResistHint: Resistance during the period (%). Elements left blank keep the value in the enemy settings.
dps.stateInvalid: Periods whose end is not after the start, and resistance changes with no resistance entered, are not used in the calculation.
dps.notRunnable: Some elements cannot run in gcsim (resolve them first)
dps.colEnergyWaitsTitle: Average number of times a burst could not be used for lack of energy and had to wait. Per lap = count ÷ (rotation loops − 1). Divisor: {{laps}}
dps.energyWaitsTotal: Burst energy waits: {{n}} per lap (all characters; count ÷ {{laps}} laps)
dps.energyWaitsNoLap: Burst energy waits: cannot be shown per lap with 1 loop (set loops to 2 or more)
dps.colEnergyWaitSecondsTitle: Average time spent per burst energy wait: from the burst coming off cooldown until enough energy has built up and it goes off (cooldown waits are not included). Total wait time ÷ number of waits across all runs. Shown as '-' when no wait occurred
dps.energyWaitSecondsTotal: Burst energy waits: {{n}} s per wait on average (all characters; cooldown waits not included)
dps.stats: HP {{hp}} / ATK {{atk}} / DEF {{def}} / EM {{em}} / CRIT {{cr}}·{{cd}} / ER {{er}}
dps.buildNote: Stats are the final values at the start (weapon, artifacts and tentative values included; buffs applied during the rotation are not). "Tentative" means a slot that does not use an owned build.
dps.loopsNote: DPS = total damage ÷ time (opening + N loops). Default 5; 1–{{max}}. The opening is included, so with few loops it has a larger effect.
dps.runsNote: How many times to run with different seeds (default 100; 1–{{max}}). More runs reduce the spread but take longer.
dps.enemiesNote: Up to {{max}} enemies, all at the same position, so AoE hits every enemy. Resistances are in % (negative allowed). Starting elemental application on enemies cannot be set in a gcsim config (apply it with attacks in the rotation).
dps.note:
- Time runs from 0 s to the later of the last action start and the last damage.
- Totals are the damage events (including reactions and extra damage) in the gcsim {{version}} detailed log.
- Real fights differ (enemy movement, missed actions, etc.).
dps.energyNoteOn: A burst without enough energy waits until it is ready (the rotation takes longer). Energy comes from Energy Recharge, skill particles and enemy particles. Enemy particles use the same default as the ER calculator (1 every 5-8 s); set the amount to 0 for none.
dps.energyNoteOff: Burst energy is ignored (the ideal case where bursts are always available, the same assumption as the timing calculation in this app). DPS is higher than in real fights.
dps.notRunnableUnknown: The config could not be built (the cause is unknown). Check the party and the rotation.
dps.stale: The party or the rotation has changed. This result is from before the change.
dps.truncated: Of the {{loops}} rotation loops, the shortest run was cut off at loop {{worst}} ({{count}} of {{runs}} runs; the energy may have run short). The DPS covers only what could be executed.
